options: The sun rise in the east.
The sun is rose in the east.
The sun rises in the east.
questions.rule: A general truth uses the simple present. The sun is singular, so the verb takes -s: rises.
An infinitive (to + base verb) can be the subject. It is singular, so it takes is: To believe is to trust.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A fact about the moon (singular) uses does not + base verb: does not have.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After to in an infinitive, use the base verb: to hope, not to hoped.
A saying that is always true uses the simple present. Honesty is singular: is.
want is followed by an infinitive: wants to become.
who starts a clause that tells us more about a person: the boy who helped me.

chat: Why can't we see the sun at night?
options: Because the earth spin and turns away from it.
Because the earth spins and turns away from it.
Because the earth spinning and turns away from it.
questions.rule: A scientific fact uses the simple present. The earth is singular: spins and turns.

chat: What do you hope to do this summer?
questions.rule: hope is followed by an infinitive (to + base verb): I hope to learn.

options: If you will work hard, you succeed.
If you worked hard, you will succeed.
If you work hard, you will succeed.
questions.rule: First conditional: If + simple present, then will + base verb: If you work hard, you will succeed.

options: If it will rain, we stay indoors.
If it rains, we will stay indoors.
If it rain, we will stay indoors.
questions.rule: In a first conditional, the if-part takes the simple present (it rains), not will.

options: Grandpa is a man who loves stories.
Grandpa is a man which loves stories.
Grandpa is a man whom loves stories.
questions.rule: Use who for a person who does the action. which is for things; whom is not a subject.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: whose shows that something belongs to someone: a child whose eyes shone.

questions.after: the bus, you will be late for school.
questions.rule: First conditional: the if-part takes the simple present: If you miss ..., you will be late.
For a thing, use that or which: the book that Aarav gave me. who is for people.
Sayings state general truths, so they use the simple present: a kind heart never grows old.

chat: Shall we go to the park this evening?
options: Yes, if it doesn't rain, we can go.
Yes, if it won't rain, we can go.
Yes, if it don't rain, we can go.
questions.rule: The if-part uses the simple present, and it takes doesn't: if it doesn't rain.

options: He is the boy which sits next to me.
He is the boy who sits next to me.
He is the boy who sit next to me.
questions.rule: Use who for a person. The verb agrees with the boy (singular): who sits.

options: To believe in yourself is important.
To believing in yourself is important.
To believe in yourself are important.
questions.rule: The infinitive subject is to + base verb (To believe) and it takes a singular verb: is.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Facts use the simple present. Plural subjects (plants) take the verb without -s: make, need.

options: We enjoy watching the stars at night.
We enjoy to watch the stars at night.
We enjoy watch the stars at night.
questions.rule: enjoy is followed by the -ing form, not an infinitive: enjoy watching.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct conditional.
options: If I am a bird, I would fly above the clouds.
If I were a bird, I will fly above the clouds.
If I were a bird, I would fly above the clouds.
questions.rule: For an imaginary situation use If + past (were), then would + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For things that always happen, both parts use the simple present. it takes -s: it melts.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: which is for things. For a person who does the action, use who: the man who lives next door.
After let + object, use the infinitive without to: let me stay up.
The if-clause gives the condition (If you believe); the main clause gives the result.

chat: Why is it so cold in Shimla even in May?
options: The air get colder as we go higher.
The air getting colder as we go higher.
The air gets colder as we go higher.
questions.rule: A fact of nature uses the simple present. The air is singular: gets.

questions.source: I have a friend. She writes poems.
options: I have a friend who writes poems.
I have a friend which writes poems.
I have a friend who write poems.
questions.rule: who replaces She and joins the sentences. The verb still agrees with a friend: writes.

questions.source: If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
options: Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you will hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
questions.rule: Unless means if ... not, so drop the not: Unless you hurry.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: People take who (my uncle, who; everyone who). Things take that/which: the roses that he grows.

options: The teacher said that the earth move round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moving round the sun.
questions.rule: In reported speech, a universal truth stays in the simple present: the earth moves round the sun.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: managed already shows the past. The infinitive after it is always to + base verb: to learn.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The main subject is Neha (singular), so the present perfect uses has: Neha ... has gone.

questions.after: every day, they will grow into strong plants.
questions.rule: Even in the passive, the if-part of a first conditional uses the simple present: are watered.

questions.after: book we are reading has won many prizes.
questions.rule: The book belongs to the poet, so use whose: the poet whose book we are reading.
too + adjective + infinitive: never too late to begin again.

chat: What would you do if you found a wallet on the road?
options: I would give it to the police.
I will gave it to the police.
I would gave it to the police.
questions.rule: An imaginary would question gets a would + base verb answer: I would give.

questions.source: Our teacher said, "Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius."
options: Our teacher said that water boiling at 100 degrees Celsius.
Our teacher said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
Our teacher said that water boil at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.rule: A scientific fact keeps its simple present tense in reported speech: water boils.

questions.source: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
options: The box is so heavy that I cannot lift it.
The box is so heavy that I can lift it.
The box is so heavy that I cannot lift.
questions.rule: too ... to becomes so ... that + a negative (cannot), and lift needs its object it.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The if-part uses the simple present: it rains; Rohan and I is plural, so finish.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct conditional.
options: If I were the captain, I will choose Meera first.
If I were the captain, I would choose Meera first.
If I am the captain, I would choose Meera first.
questions.rule: Imaginary present: If I were ... I would + base verb. Don't mix were with will or am with would.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A clause between commas only adds extra information. It uses which for things, never that.

questions.after: next, the old man sat down and waited for dawn.
questions.rule: After question words like what, how or where, use an infinitive: what to do.
that starts a clause describing a language: a language that everyone can understand.

chat: What did the scientist tell your class about light?
options: She told us that light travels faster than sound.
She told us that light travel faster than sound.
She told to us that light travels faster than sound.
questions.rule: A fact stays in the simple present after told (light travels), and told takes no to: told us.

chat: Why did you go to the library?
options: I went there for return the books.
I went there to returning the books.
I went there to return the books.
questions.rule: To give a purpose, use an infinitive: to return. Not for return or to returning.

questions.source: I am not a bird, so I cannot fly.
options: If I was a bird, I can fly.
If I were a bird, I could fly.
If I am a bird, I could fly.
questions.rule: An unreal present becomes If + past (were) and could/would + base verb: I could fly.

questions.source: I know an old man. His stories make everyone smile.
options: I know an old man whose stories make everyone smile.
I know an old man whose his stories make everyone smile.
I know an old man who's stories make everyone smile.
questions.rule: whose replaces His, so don't keep both. who's means who is.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: An infinitive subject is singular (means); every day is singular (gives); after to use the base verb (begin).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Things take that (the strength that lies); a person as subject takes who; a smile is singular: keeps.
